description: Unofficial Cloudflare WARP MASQUE Client for Windows, macOS, Linux and Android: system VPN, SOCKS5 and HTTP proxy over MASQUE, with chain proxy and routing rules.

## Usque v0.3.5 official release / Usque v0.3.5 正式版发布 Usque v0.3.5 brings Usque to macOS, makes connection scenes easier to switch, and adds more control over your connections. Usque v0.3.5 将 Usque 带到 macOS，简化连接场景切换，并提供更灵活的连接设置。 ## Highlights / 更新亮点 ✨ - **Usque for macOS** — Use Usque on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs running macOS 13 or later.
**macOS 版 Usque** — 现在可以在运行 macOS 13 或更高版本的 Apple Silicon 与 Intel Mac 上使用 Usque。 - **Connection multiplexing** — Choose multiple connections in advanced network settings to increase overall throughput when several apps or downloads are active.
**连接多路复用** — 在高级网络设置中启用多条连接，多个应用或下载同时进行时可提升整体网络吞吐速率。 - **Simpler scene switching** — Find and switch your preferred connection scenes more easily from Profiles.
**更便捷的场景切换** — 在“配置”中更轻松地查找和切换常用连接场景。 - **Smoother Windows recovery** — Improved recovery when a network adapter is no longer available.
**更顺畅的 Windows 恢复** — 改进网络适配器不可用时的恢复体验。 - **Everyday refinements** — Polished connection settings and the experience across devices.
**日常体验改进** — 完善连接设置并优化多设备使用体验。 ## Download / 下载 📥 | Platform / 平台 | Download / 下载 | | :---: | :---: | | ![Windows](https://github.com/GeorgeXie2333/usque-app/blob/v0.3.5/docs/assets/release/windows.svg?raw=true)

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Русский · فارسی

An unofficial client compatible with Cloudflare® WARP® services for Windows, macOS, Linux and Android / Android TV,
with a native Flutter interface and a Rust MASQUE engine.

An independent project. Not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Cloudflare, Inc.

Windows

Android

English interface previews rendered from the current source with sample data.

## Overview - **Performance** — a Rust MASQUE engine over HTTP/3 with automatic HTTP/2 fallback, batched UDP I/O on Android and Linux, a larger UDP receive buffer on Windows and Android, and selectable congestion control including BBRv2 and experimental BBRv3. - **VPN and local proxies** — system VPN (TUN), SOCKS5 and HTTP proxy share one WARP connection and can run together. - **Chain proxy** — leave WARP through OpenVPN, WireGuard, Proton VPN, VPN Gate, HTTP or SOCKS5. - **Routing and ad blocking** — DIRECT / REJECT / PROXY rules for domains and CIDRs, Ads rules and country-based direct routing. - **Encrypted DNS** — DoH or DoT for the WARP exit and for direct-rule queries. - **Network diagnostics** — latency, packet loss and 60-second trends, with deep checks only after confirmation. - **Scenes** — save common network setups in **Profiles** and switch between them. - **Privacy** — a server-key check that cannot be skipped, system credential stores, redacted local diagnostics and no analytics. - **Platform integration** — Windows tray, Android Quick Settings tile and TV navigation; 21 languages with light and dark themes. ## Screens

Scenes
Switch saved network setups
Chain proxy
OpenVPN, WireGuard and proxy exits
Bypass settings
Direct, block or proxy by rule
Network quality
Latency, loss and throughput
## How it works Apps reach Usque through the VPN or proxies you turn on. Usque carries their traffic to WARP over MASQUE, where it leaves directly or through an optional chain exit. Explicit direct rules send matching traffic through your current network instead. ```mermaid flowchart LR apps["Apps and system traffic"] usque(["Usque"]) warp["WARP"] chain["Optional chain exit
OpenVPN · WireGuard
Proton VPN · VPN Gate
HTTP · SOCKS5"] local["Current network"] net(("Internet")) apps -->|"VPN/TUN
SOCKS5 · HTTP"| usque usque -->|"MASQUE
HTTP/3 · HTTP/2"| warp warp --> net warp -.-> chain -.-> net usque -.->|"DIRECT rules"| local -.-> net classDef brand fill:#C2500C,stroke:#C2500C,color:#ffffff class usque brand ``` ## Download Version **v0.3.5** adds macOS desktop support and configurable parallel connections, and makes scenes easier to switch. For an installed version, follow its release notes and the documentation at its tag. | Platform | Minimum system | Package | | --- | --- | --- | | Windows | Windows 10 2004, build 19041 | x64-v2 or ARM64 installer EXE | | macOS | macOS 13 or later | DMGs for Apple Silicon (arm64) and Intel (x86_64) | | Linux (since v0.3.3) | Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, supported Fedora; systemd | amd64 or arm64 AppImage, deb or rpm | | Android / Android TV | Android 8.0, API 26 | arm64-v8a, x86_64 or armeabi-v7a APK, or the universal APK | Windows x64 requires a CPU supporting **x86-64-v2**; ARM64 Windows uses the native ARM64 package. When the Android ABI is unknown, use the larger universal APK, which contains all three ABIs. Each release also includes two Windows MSI files reserved for in-app updates; install Windows manually with the EXE. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Download official packages only from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/GeorgeXie2333/usque-app/releases).** Pull Request artifacts, local builds, and untagged binaries are not official. > > **Verify before installing.** Compare the package SHA-256 with `SHA256SUMS` and GitHub's asset digest, then verify the signer fingerprint published in the release notes. On Linux, also verify the Ed25519 manifest. Stop if any value differs. > > **Never bypass a warning.** Pre-1.0 Windows and Android packages use fixed, project-controlled self-signed certificates: Windows may show an unknown-publisher warning, and Android packages are installed outside Google Play. Do not disable antivirus or the firewall, or import certificates from unofficial packages, to bypass a warning. - **Upgrades migrate configuration one way.** v0.3.2 and v0.3.3 use configuration schema 26; upgrading from v0.3.1 migrates schema 24 to 26, which v0.3.1 and older clients cannot read. v0.3.4 migrates schema 26 to 27, which v0.3.3 and older clients cannot read. Reinstalling an older package does not reverse the migration, so review [configuration compatibility](docs/INSTALLATION.md#configuration-compatibility-when-upgrading) and any required pre-upgrade backup first. v0.3.5 migrates to schema 28, which v0.3.4 and older clients cannot read. - **Linux:** the first AppImage VPN setup installs a background service with administrator authorization, and credentials require an unlocked Secret Service keyring. The [Linux desktop guide](docs/LINUX_DESKTOP.md) covers GNOME/KDE, X11/Wayland, recovery and the tested coverage. - **Updates** require confirmation before downloading and use the platform installer; there is no unattended installation. - [Installation and removal](docs/INSTALLATION.md) covers upgrades, uninstall, recovery and Android developer verification; [Code signing](docs/CODE_SIGNING.md) lists the official identities. ## Quick start 1. Install a [verified official package](docs/INSTALLATION.md#verify-before-installing) and open Usque. 2. Complete the first-run permissions and terms steps, then register a Consumer WARP® account, optionally with a WARP License Key. If setup was interrupted, check the saved result before registering again. Usque does not accept new WARP Secret imports. 3. Open **Proxy**. Turn on **TUN** (Windows/Linux) or **VPN** (Android) under **Device traffic**, and the **SOCKS5 proxy** or **HTTP proxy** switch at the top of its own section, then connect from **Home**. Android setup requests only optional notifications. VPN authorization is requested when connecting with VPN output and may disconnect another VPN; proxy-only connections do not request it. These switches take effect immediately; listener address and port edits require **Apply changes**. | Connection option | When to use it | | --- | --- | | VPN/TUN | Route system traffic through the tunnel, with your bypass and Android per-app rules. | | SOCKS5 | Give compatible applications a local TCP/UDP proxy; remote DNS is the default. | | HTTP proxy | Give compatible applications a local HTTP proxy, including HTTPS through CONNECT. | | System proxy (Windows/Linux) | Point Windows or GNOME/KDE proxy settings at Usque's HTTP proxy; HTTP output must be enabled. | VPN, SOCKS5 and HTTP are enabled by default; system proxy is off. They share one WARP connection and can run together. Turning off every output keeps the WARP connection open, but no app traffic uses it. Each account stores its own credentials; only one account connects at a time. Network settings are shared by all accounts. ## Features ### Performance and transport - **Throughput:** the engine batches UDP sends and receives (`sendmmsg`/`recvmmsg`) on Android and Linux, requests a larger [UDP receive buffer](docs/UDP_RECEIVE_BUFFER.md) on Windows and Android, and offers [selectable HTTP/3 congestion control](docs/congestion-control.md): Cubic by default, BBRv2, experimental BBRv3 and Reno. - **Automatic transport:** HTTP/3 with HTTP/2 fallback. IPv4 and IPv6 connection attempts help find a reachable endpoint, and supported H3 network changes can migrate the connection. See [path behavior](docs/h3-path-infrastructure.md). - **[Experimental L4 mode](docs/L4_PROXY.md)** (opt-in) proxies TCP over HTTP/3. Without an OpenVPN TCP chain, it does not forward ordinary UDP, so applications that need UDP may not work. Auto does not select L4. ### Scenes and accounts - **[Local connection scenes](docs/SCENARIOS.md)** in **Profiles** save account binding, chain proxy, endpoints, endpoint IP preference and transport. Review changes before use and restore the latest switch; the TUN/VPN and proxy switches, routing and DNS stay global. Saving a scene does not change the running connection, and saved and applied states remain distinct. Accounts are under **Manage accounts → Accounts**. - **WARP login information export:** after confirmation, export your Consumer WARP login information (WARP Secret) to a file you choose. Usque cannot import that file to restore the account after reinstalling. ### Chain proxy - Open **Proxy → Chain proxy** to leave WARP through **OpenVPN**, **WireGuard**, [**WARP via WireGuard**](docs/WARP_WIREGUARD.md), [**Proton VPN**](docs/PROTON_VPN.md), **VPN Gate**, **HTTP** or **SOCKS5**. Import a VPN configuration or add a proxy server, then select and apply one. Off by default; see the [chain proxy guide](docs/CHAIN_PROXY.md). - VPN, SOCKS5 and HTTP share the exit; explicit direct rules still apply. - Native Proton setup is under validation; live sign-in, the human puzzle and the full tunnel remain untested. ### Routing, blocking and DNS - Full-tunnel VPN, tunneled DNS, Kill Switch, LAN access and [DIRECT/REJECT/PROXY routing rules with Ads](docs/ROUTING.md). Custom domains and CIDRs support more-specific exceptions; conflicts are checked before saving. - Custom routing-rule edits apply to new flows during a stable connection without reconnecting. Existing TCP/CONNECT streams and active UDP targets retain their paths; check the apply result for pending or failed changes. - Ads rules are prepared automatically when enabled and applied, checked every seven days while the app runs, and take effect on new requests without reconnecting. **Rule details** provides status, source and manual updates. - Optional country-based direct routing downloads the selected countries' GeoIP data and the global GeoSite catalog separately. Usque uses domain rules when the name is visible, otherwise IP rules; unknown destinations stay in the tunnel. - Custom [WARP exit DNS](docs/WARP_DNS.md): open **Settings → Advanced network settings → WARP DNS**, choose Plain DNS, DoH or DoT, and select **Apply changes**. Changing DNS reconnects an established session; the final chain exit keeps its own DNS policy. ### Diagnostics - Local [network diagnostics](docs/network-doctor.md) and a **Network Quality** page showing latency, packet-loss readings and availability, queues and 60-second trends. Standard checks read local state; Deep checks send test requests only after confirmation. ### Desktop and Android - **Windows:** tray with a status badge and TUN and system-proxy switches; background notifications for a reconnect lasting five seconds, a connection error, and recovery after a reported interruption; single-instance activation, start on boot, close-to-tray and a remembered window position. **Ctrl+1–4** selects pages, **Ctrl+S** applies changes, and **F5** refreshes VPN Gate or diagnostics. See [tray and keyboard controls](docs/INSTALLATION.md#tray-and-keyboard-controls). - **Android:** Quick Settings tile, launcher shortcuts, boot recovery and TV navigation. - **Android per-app proxy** applies to the whole app, across accounts. When off, all apps use the VPN. When on, only selected apps do; newly installed apps must be selected. With Android **Block connections without VPN**, unselected apps are blocked instead of bypassing the tunnel. - **Everywhere:** twenty-one languages, with light and dark themes. ## Privacy and security - **Verified server.** Usque requires the WARP server's public key to match the registered key. There is no option to skip this check. - **Protected credentials.** Credentials stay in Windows Credential Manager, the Linux Secret Service keyring or Android Keystore. Windows and Linux use a separate Agent for privileged network operations; Android runs the VPN in a dedicated process. - **Local proxies.** Proxies listen on loopback by default. SOCKS5 and HTTP support optional username/password authentication; without configured credentials they require no authentication. Proxy-only mode does not provide a system-wide VPN Kill Switch. - **No analytics.** Diagnostics are generated locally and redacted. There is no usage analytics or automatic upload, and quality history stays in memory. Logs default to INFO and are limited to 7 days or 20 MiB. Do not post credentials or raw diagnostic bundles in public Issues; report vulnerabilities through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ### Limits - Android's in-app Kill Switch cannot protect traffic after the VPN process dies. VPN Gate terminal failures also end the connection. To keep apps blocked after the VPN ends, enable both system **Always-on VPN** and **Block connections without VPN**. See [Android setup](docs/INSTALLATION.md#android-and-android-tv). - Usque does not combine several paths for extra bandwidth. Some quality readings, including HTTP/2 packet loss and PMTU, are unavailable. Local diagnostics cannot detect traffic leaks. ### DNS privacy - **Direct rules use your current network's DNS by default.** Country-based and custom-domain direct rules use **Current network DNS**: matching domain queries go to the DNS servers on your current network, outside the VPN. You can instead choose **DoH** with a full HTTPS URL or **DoT** with a server name and port. New drafts prefill Cloudflare; saved custom settings are preserved. That resolver receives the queries; connection failures do not switch them to plaintext DNS. See [configuration steps and examples](docs/encrypted-direct-dns.md). - **Other remote VPN queries** use the WARP tunnel or the selected final chain exit. HTTP/SOCKS5 chain DNS defaults to verified Cloudflare® DoH through that proxy; custom or non-default inherited DNS retains TCP DNS. With these exits, application-selected UDP/53 queries use TCP to that resolver, with no physical DNS fallback. See the [chain DNS choices](docs/CHAIN_PROXY.md#http-and-socks5-exits--http-与-socks5-出口). - **Apps that use their own encrypted DNS** hide domain names from Usque, so direct routing uses IP rules. - Rule downloads also respect Android Lockdown and any remaining Windows Kill Switch while disconnected. ### Experimental and unsupported [Zero Trust enrollment](docs/ZERO_TRUST_EXPERIMENTAL.md) is experimental. It uses an organization identity for the MASQUE Internet tunnel and does not provide full Cloudflare One™ Client compatibility. iOS, store distribution and a public CLI are outside this release's scope. ### macOS in v0.3.5 The macOS version supports local HTTP and SOCKS5 proxies on macOS 13 and later. System-wide TUN remains disabled in release DMGs. See the [macOS feature matrix](docs/MACOS_WINDOWS_PARITY.md) and [installation guide](docs/INSTALLATION.md#choose-a-package). Historical **unofficial v0.3.3 dev pre-release** for macOS 13+: [Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/JustinL330/usque-app/releases/download/macos-dev-v0.3.3-compact-12636756/usque-v0.3.3-macos-arm64.dmg) or [Intel (x86_64)](https://github.com/JustinL330/usque-app/releases/download/macos-dev-v0.3.3-compact-12636756/usque-v0.3.3-macos-x86_64.dmg). These ad-hoc signed packages are not notarized or production releases. Read the [release notes, checksums and manifests](https://github.com/JustinL330/usque-app/releases/tag/macos-dev-v0.3.3-compact-12636756) before testing; system VPN activation remains disabled. The compact images reduce downloads by 46.6% / 43.2%; see the [size explanation and validation](docs/MACOS_PACKAGE_SIZE.md). These older downloads include CEF verification and all application languages. The historical downloads above predate current macOS scenes and recovery. macOS supports Proton account sign-in, but not guest registration or the embedded verification browser; import a Proton configuration when browser verification is required. Use official releases for current packages. The [macOS test checklist](docs/MACOS_QA_CHECKLIST.md) separates isolated tests from actual device acceptance. The following items remain open: - **System VPN/TUN:** ordinary DMGs keep it disabled. The Agent still requires device acceptance for routing, DNS and Kill Switch protection. Proxy-only mode protects traffic that applications send to the proxy. - **System proxy and chain exits:** isolated configuration, recovery and transport tests do not establish a successful live connection. Real authorization and each external exit still need device tests. Current macOS source reuses WARP or opens a temporary WARP connection for VPN Gate, retaining saved chain settings; direct physical-network catalogue fallback remains disabled. - **Zero Trust:** callback validation and cancel/retry tests use synthetic data; an actual organization login and callback remain unverified. - **Proton accounts:** macOS has no guest registration or embedded verification browser. Account sign-in, authenticator codes and saved-account management remain available; live sign-in and traffic still require device testing. - **Desktop and hardware:** layout checks use headless Windows/macOS widget renders. Actual native-window interaction, Intel execution and macOS 13 hardware remain untested. The default Mac content area now matches Windows at 1040×760, fits the available screen, and preserves saved window geometry. No application, browser, permission window or host network setting is opened or changed by this background validation. Development packages are not notarized. ## Default network settings | Setting | Default | | --- | --- | | Consumer endpoint selection | Automatic selection; existing configurations retain Custom | | Saved custom endpoint IPv4 | `162.159.198.2` | | Saved custom endpoint IPv6 | `2606:4700:103::2` | | Port / SNI | `443` / `speed.cloudflare.com` | | Transport | Auto: HTTP/3, then HTTP/2 | | HTTP/3 congestion control | `cubic`; BBRv2, experimental BBRv3, and `reno` are selectable | | MASQUE multiplexed connections | `1`; manually configurable from `1` to `8` for HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 / L4 | | QUIC UDP receive buffer | [2 MiB target](docs/UDP_RECEIVE_BUFFER.md) on Windows/Android for H3 and L4; actual capacity is OS-dependent | | TUN MTU | `1280` | | Fallback DNS | `1.1.1.1`, `2606:4700:4700::1111` | | SOCKS5 | `127.0.0.1:1080`, `[::1]:1080` | | HTTP proxy | `127.0.0.1:8080`, `[::1]:8080` |
How proxy, endpoint and congestion-control changes apply
Proxy address and port edits are drafts until applied. Proxy DNS uses the current exit by default: configure [WARP DNS](docs/WARP_DNS.md) in Advanced settings or the final DNS in the chain configuration. The Proxy page has no DNS settings; a proxy DNS choice saved by an older version keeps working. Advanced settings reset loads defaults into the draft; it does not apply them immediately. In **Advanced network settings → MASQUE multiplexed connections**, enter **1–8** (default **1**), then **Apply changes**. A changed count reconnects the session. Separate flows use different MASQUE connections; each flow stays on one connection. The setting applies to HTTP/2/HTTP/3 CONNECT-IP and L4 (HTTP/3 TCP CONNECT). See [connection behavior](docs/NETWORK_SETTINGS.md#parallel-masque-connections). In Advanced network settings, Automatic selection races eligible account endpoints; Custom keeps manual addresses. Port and SNI remain editable. See [automatic endpoints](docs/NETWORK_SETTINGS.md#automatic-endpoints--自动选择端点). Zero Trust endpoint addresses start with registered values. In Advanced network settings, choose **Edit Zero Trust endpoints**, read the red fullscreen warning and acknowledge the risks and your authorization before editing IPv4/IPv6; then **Apply changes**. Reset stages the registered addresses; signing in again restores them and removes custom addresses. Home keeps a risk notice visible while the selected account has custom Zero Trust addresses or a running ZT session still uses them; the notice cannot be dismissed. Congestion-control changes are saved for the next manual connection or retry, not applied to the current session or its automatic reconnections. HTTP/2 uses system TCP. See [HTTP/3 congestion control](docs/congestion-control.md).
## Documentation and development Start with the [Wiki](https://github.com/GeorgeXie2333/usque-app/wiki/Home) for setup and practical tutorials. Use the [documentation index](docs/README.md) for the complete reference; most technical documents are in English. | Need | Read | | --- | --- | | Install, update, uninstall, or recover | [Installation](docs/INSTALLATION.md) | | Native Proton guest/account setup | [Proton VPN guide and current limits](docs/PROTON_VPN.md) | | Connect to Proton VPN through the WARP tunnel | [WireGuard over MASQUE tutorial](https://github.com/GeorgeXie2333/usque-app/wiki/Proton-VPN-over-MASQUE) | | Understand local quality checks | [Network Doctor](docs/network-doctor.md) | | Build and test changes safely | [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) | | Understand implementation and verification status | [Implementation](docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md) | | Maintain an official release | [Release process](docs/RELEASE.md) | Use the pinned toolchains and change-scoped checks in the contribution guide. Compile-only builds and deterministic tests are safe workstation checks; installing development packages or exercising VPN lifecycle requires the designated isolated environments. ## Upstream and license Protocol behavior follows [Diniboy1123/usque](https://github.com/Diniboy1123/usque). This repository keeps a snapshot of that client in `oracle/go` for interoperability tests. The Flutter UI and Rust engine are new code. Upstream copyright stays in the license. First-party source is [MIT](LICENSE.md). Third-party components keep their own licenses. The optional [chain proxy](docs/CHAIN_PROXY.md) embeds OpenVPN 3 Core under MPL-2.0 and Mbed TLS under Apache-2.0. Corresponding source, reviewed patches and license texts are included in `third_party`; the application exposes the notices from its VPN Gate page. WireGuard uses BoringTun 0.7.1 (BSD-3-Clause), and local SVG icons use flutter_svg 2.3.4 (MIT); their notices are in the app's license registry. The independent Proton SRP implementation references Proton go-srp (MIT); its [copyright and full license](apps/usque_gui/assets/licenses/proton-srp.txt) are retained in source, test vectors and the app license registry. --- Usque is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Cloudflare, Inc. Use of consumer WARP services remains subject to Cloudflare's terms and privacy policy. Cloudflare, WARP and Cloudflare One are trademarks and/or registered trademarks of Cloudflare, Inc. in the United States and other jurisdictions.

## 概览 - **性能** — Rust 编写的 MASQUE 引擎，基于 HTTP/3 并自动回退到 HTTP/2；Android 与 Linux 批量收发 UDP，Windows 与 Android 申请更大的 UDP 接收缓冲，拥塞控制可选 BBRv2 和实验性 BBRv3。 - **VPN 与本地代理** — 系统 VPN（虚拟网卡）、SOCKS5 和 HTTP 代理共用一条 WARP 连接，可以同时使用。 - **链式代理** — 在 WARP 之后经 OpenVPN、WireGuard、Proton VPN、VPN Gate、HTTP 或 SOCKS5 出口访问网络。 - **分流与广告拦截** — 针对域名和 CIDR 的 DIRECT／REJECT／PROXY 规则、Ads 广告拦截和按国家直连。 - **加密 DNS** — WARP 出口和直连规则的域名查询都可以使用 DoH 或 DoT。 - **网络诊断** — 延迟、丢包和最近 60 秒趋势；深度检查需要你确认后才会执行。 - **场景** — 在 **配置** 页保存常用网络配置并随时切换。 - **隐私** — 强制校验服务端公钥，凭据存放在系统凭据库，诊断在本地生成并脱敏，不做使用统计。 - **平台集成** — Windows 托盘、Android 快捷设置磁贴和电视遥控器导航；21 种语言，浅色、深色主题。 ## 界面一览

**吞吐：** 引擎在 Android 和 Linux 上批量收发 UDP（`sendmmsg`/`recvmmsg`），在 Windows 和 Android 上申请更大的 [UDP 接收缓冲](docs/UDP_RECEIVE_BUFFER.md)，并提供[可选的 HTTP/3 拥塞控制](docs/congestion-control.md)：默认 Cubic，另有 BBRv2、实验性 BBRv3 和 Reno。 - **自动传输：** 先尝试 HTTP/3，失败时回退到 HTTP/2，并尝试通过 IPv4 和 IPv6 寻找可达端点；H3 在支持的网络切换场景下可以迁移连接，详见[路径行为](docs/h3-path-infrastructure.md)。 - **[实验性 L4 模式](docs/L4_PROXY.md)**（需手动启用）通过 HTTP/3 代理 TCP 流量。未启用 OpenVPN TCP 链式出口时，它不转发普通 UDP 流量，需要 UDP 的应用可能无法正常使用。自动模式不会选择 L4。 ### 场景与账号 - **[本机网络场景](docs/SCENARIOS.md)**在 **配置** 页保存账号绑定、链式代理、端点、端点 IP 偏好与传输协议。可预览后使用，并恢复最近一次切换；虚拟网卡与代理开关、分流与 DNS 保持全局。保存场景不改变当前连接，页面明确区分已保存和已应用。账号在 **账号管理 → 账号** 中管理。 - **导出 WARP 登录信息：** 确认后可将个人版 WARP 登录信息（WARP Secret）导出到指定文件。Usque 目前无法重新导入该文件，因此它不能用于重装后的账号恢复。 ### 链式代理 - 在 **代理 → 链式代理** 中选择 **OpenVPN**、**WireGuard**、[**WARP via WireGuard**](docs/WARP_WIREGUARD.md)、[**Proton VPN**](docs/PROTON_VPN.md)、**VPN Gate**、**HTTP** 或 **SOCKS5** 作为 WARP 之后的出口。VPN 配置支持文件或文本导入，HTTP/SOCKS5 通过表单添加，保存后选用并应用。此功能默认关闭，详见[链式代理指南](docs/CHAIN_PROXY.md)。 - VPN、SOCKS5 和 HTTP 共用最终出口，显式直连规则仍然生效。 - 原生 Proton 来源仍在验证中；实网登录、真人拼图和完整隧道尚未实测。 ### 分流、拦截与 DNS - 全隧道 VPN、隧道内 DNS、Kill Switch（断网保护）、局域网访问和 [DIRECT／REJECT／PROXY 分流及 Ads 广告拦截](docs/ROUTING.md)。自定义域名、IP 和 CIDR 支持更具体的例外规则，保存时检查冲突。 - 连接稳定时，自定义分流规则直接用于新流，无需重连；已有 TCP／CONNECT 连接和活跃 UDP 目标保持原路径。请查看应用结果，确认是否仍待应用或应用失败。 - 开启广告拦截并应用后自动准备规则，应用运行期间每 7 天检查更新，新请求无需重连即可生效；**规则详情** 提供状态、来源和手动更新。 - 可选的按国家直连：单独下载所选国家的 GeoIP 数据和全局 GeoSite 域名规则。能看到域名时按域名判断，否则按 IP 判断；无法识别的目标继续走隧道。 - 自定义 [WARP 出口 DNS](docs/WARP_DNS.md)：打开 **设置 → 高级网络设置 → WARP DNS**，选择普通 DNS、DoH 或 DoT，再点击 **应用修改**。修改 DNS 会重新连接当前会话；最终链式出口仍使用自己的 DNS 策略。 ### 诊断 - 本地[网络诊断](docs/network-doctor.md)和 **网络质量** 页面，展示延迟、丢包率及其测量状态、队列和最近 60 秒的趋势。**标准** 检查只读取本地状态；**深度** 检查会在你确认后发送测试请求。 ### 桌面与 Android - **Windows：** 托盘提供状态角标、虚拟网卡与系统代理开关；窗口在后台时，持续五秒的重连、连接错误和已通知中断后的恢复会弹出通知；另支持单实例、开机启动、关闭窗口后最小化到托盘和记住窗口位置。**Ctrl+1～4** 切换页面，**Ctrl+S** 应用修改，**F5** 刷新 VPN Gate 或诊断。详见[托盘与快捷键操作](docs/INSTALLATION.md#tray-and-keyboard-controls)。 - **Android：** 快捷设置磁贴、启动器快捷方式、开机恢复和电视遥控器导航。 - **Android 分应用代理** 对所有账号生效。关闭时，所有应用都使用 VPN；开启后，只有勾选的应用使用 VPN，新安装的应用需要手动勾选。如果同时启用了系统的“屏蔽未使用 VPN 的所有连接”，未勾选的应用将无法联网。 - **全平台：** 提供 21 种语言，以及浅色、深色主题。 ## 隐私与安全 - **校验服务端。** 强制校验 WARP 服务端公钥，不提供跳过校验的选项。 - **保护凭据。** 凭据保存在 Windows 凭据管理器、Linux Secret Service 钥匙串或 Android Keystore 中。Windows 和 Linux 由独立 Agent 执行需要管理员权限的网络操作；Android 使用独立的 VPN 进程。 - **本机代理。** 代理默认仅供本机使用。SOCKS5 和 HTTP 支持可选的用户名、密码认证；未配置凭据时不要求认证。仅使用代理不能提供系统级 VPN 断网保护。 - **不做统计。** 诊断在本地生成并脱敏，不进行用户行为统计，也不自动上传。网络质量历史只保留在内存中。日志默认为 INFO，最多保留 7 天或 20 MiB。不要将凭据或原始诊断包放入公开 Issue；漏洞请通过 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) 私密报告。 ### 限制 - Android 应用内的断网保护无法在 VPN 进程结束后继续工作。VPN Gate 无法继续连接时，也会断开 VPN。如果需要在 VPN 结束后继续阻止应用联网，请同时开启系统的“始终开启的 VPN”和“屏蔽未使用 VPN 的所有连接”。操作方法见 [Android 安装说明](docs/INSTALLATION.md#android-and-android-tv)。 - Usque 不会通过多条路径叠加带宽。部分指标无法测量，例如 HTTP/2 的丢包率和 PMTU。本地诊断无法检测流量泄漏。 ### DNS 隐私 - **直连规则默认使用当前网络的 DNS。** 按国家及自定义域名直连默认使用 **当前网络的 DNS**：匹配规则的域名查询会发送给当前网络使用的 DNS 服务器，位于 VPN 隧道之外。也可以选择 **DoH** 并填写完整 HTTPS 地址，或选择 **DoT** 并填写服务器域名和端口。新草稿预填 Cloudflare，已保存的自定义配置保持不变。查询会发送给该服务器；连接失败时不会改用明文 DNS。详见[配置步骤与示例](docs/encrypted-direct-dns.md)。 - **其他远程 VPN 查询**使用 WARP 隧道或所选最终链式出口。HTTP/SOCKS5 链 DNS 默认经该代理使用校验 TLS 的 Cloudflare® DoH；自定义或非默认继承 DNS 保留 TCP。在这两种出口下，应用指定的 UDP/53 查询转换为发往该解析器的 TCP，不回退到物理 DNS。详见[链 DNS 选择](docs/CHAIN_PROXY.md#http-and-socks5-exits--http-与-socks5-出口)。 - **应用自行使用加密 DNS 时**，Usque 看不到域名，此时按 IP 判断是否直连。 - 断开连接后下载规则，也仍受 Android 系统阻断设置和尚未解除的 Windows 断网保护约束。 ### 实验性功能与支持范围 [Zero Trust 注册](docs/ZERO_TRUST_EXPERIMENTAL.md)仍属实验性功能：可以用组织身份建立 MASQUE 公网隧道， 但不提供完整的 Cloudflare One™ Client 功能。 当前也不提供 iOS 版本、应用商店分发或公开命令行工具。 ### v0.3.5 的 macOS 支持 v0.3.5 的 macOS 版支持在 macOS 13 及以上版本使用本地 HTTP 和 SOCKS5 代理，正式 DMG 不启用系统级 VPN。详见 [macOS 功能对照表](docs/MACOS_WINDOWS_PARITY.md)和[安装指南](docs/INSTALLATION.md#choose-a-package)。 macOS 13+ **历史 v0.3.3 非官方 dev 预发布包**： [Apple Silicon（arm64）](https://github.com/JustinL330/usque-app/releases/download/macos-dev-v0.3.3-compact-12636756/usque-v0.3.3-macos-arm64.dmg)／ [Intel（x86_64）](https://github.com/JustinL330/usque-app/releases/download/macos-dev-v0.3.3-compact-12636756/usque-v0.3.3-macos-x86_64.dmg)。 安装包仅作临时签名，尚未公证，不是正式版本，系统 VPN 保持关闭。测试前请阅读 [发布说明、校验值和清单](https://github.com/JustinL330/usque-app/releases/tag/macos-dev-v0.3.3-compact-12636756)。 上述旧版精简包下载量减少约 47%／43%，包含繁体中文、原有界面语言、CEF 验证元件和 sandbox。 体积原因与验证结果见[macOS 安装包体积说明](docs/MACOS_PACKAGE_SIZE.md)。 上方历史安装包早于当前连接场景及恢复功能，请使用正式 Release 获取当前安装包。 [macOS 测试清单](docs/MACOS_QA_CHECKLIST.md)分别记录隔离测试与真机验收。以下项目仍未完成： - 修改代理地址和端口后，需要点击 **应用修改** 才会提交。代理默认通过当前出口解析：在高级设置中配置 [WARP DNS](docs/WARP_DNS.md)，或在链式配置中设置最终出口 DNS。代理页不再提供 DNS 设置；旧版本保存的代理 DNS 选择继续生效。 高级设置中的重置只会填入默认值，仍需提交才会生效。 打开 **高级网络设置 → MASQUE 多路复用连接数**，填写 **1–8**（默认 **1**），再点击 **应用修改**。连接数变化会重新连接；不同流分配到不同 MASQUE 连接，同一条流固定使用一条连接。该设置适用于 HTTP/2、HTTP/3 CONNECT-IP 和 L4（HTTP/3 TCP CONNECT）。详见[连接行为](docs/NETWORK_SETTINGS.md#parallel-masque-connections)。 高级网络设置的“自动选择”会并发连接账号可用的端点；“自定义”保留手动地址。端口和 SNI 在两种模式均可修改。详见[自动选择端点](docs/NETWORK_SETTINGS.md#automatic-endpoints--自动选择端点)。 Zero Trust 端点初始使用注册地址。在高级网络设置中选择 **编辑 Zero Trust 端点**，阅读红色全屏警告，勾选确认风险及使用授权后编辑 IPv4/IPv6，再点击 **应用修改**。恢复默认会暂存注册地址；重新登录会恢复注册地址并移除自定义地址。当前账号配置自定义 Zero Trust 地址，或当前 ZT 连接仍在使用自定义地址时，首页会常驻不可关闭的风险提示。 拥塞控制的更改会保存，并在下一次手动连接或重试时生效，不影响当前会话及其自动重连。HTTP/2 使用系统 TCP。详见 [HTTP/3 拥塞控制](docs/congestion-control.md)。
